guides.title: Sudden No Service? Check for the eSIM / SIM upgrade scam
guides.summary: Scammers call as customer care, offer a SIM upgrade or eSIM, and send an activation link. If it works, your phone shows No Service and your calls, SMS and OTPs go to their eSIM. Three things to do.

steps.title: 1. Cut any SIM upgrade or eSIM call
steps.body: If a caller or message asks you to upgrade your SIM, convert to eSIM, click an activation link, scan a QR code or share an OTP, end the call and do not click. Only request an eSIM yourself, through your mobile operator's official app or store. TRAI does not call about disconnecting your number; disconnection for billing, KYC or misuse is done by your operator.

steps.title: 2. Sudden No Service that does not come back? Act at once
steps.body: From another phone, call your bank (ask them to block UPI, cards and net banking if needed) and your mobile operator's official customer care (ask whether a new SIM or eSIM was issued on your number).

steps.title: 3. Report it
steps.body: Report the suspected fraud call or SMS on Sanchar Saathi: sancharsaathi.gov.in > Chakshu (Report Suspected Fraud), within 30 days. If money was lost, call 1930 or file at cybercrime.gov.in right away.

guides.tip: Send this to parents and anyone who trusts every 'customer care' caller. A real upgrade never needs you to click a link from a caller.
guides.caution: Never share an OTP, UPI PIN or eSIM QR code with anyone who calls you, whatever name they use.

guides.title: Money leaving every month? Check and cancel unknown UPI AutoPay mandates
guides.summary: One UPI PIN on an AutoPay (mandate) request approves debits every month, not just once. Forgotten free trials and fake 'bill' requests can keep taking money. Check the live AutoPay list in your UPI app and cancel anything you do not recognise.

steps.title: Google Pay: open your AutoPay list
steps.body: Open Google Pay > tap your profile picture (top right) > Autopay. Open the Live tab: these mandates can still debit your account.

steps.title: PhonePe: open your AutoPay list
steps.body: Open PhonePe > tap your profile picture > under Payment Management, tap AutoPay. In other UPI apps look under Profile or Settings for AutoPay, Mandates or Subscriptions.

steps.title: Cancel anything you do not recognise
steps.body: Google Pay: tap the mandate in the Live tab > Cancel autopay > enter your UPI PIN. PhonePe: select the AutoPay > Remove AutoPay. You can also pause a mandate instead of cancelling it.

steps.title: From now on: check for the word Recurring
steps.body: A one-time bill (electricity, KYC fee, 'lottery tax') should never ask you to approve a Recurring or Monthly mandate. If a request from an unknown number says Recurring, tap Decline. You never need your UPI PIN to receive money.

guides.tip: Check the list once every few months, and do it on your parents' phones too. Cancelling stops future debits; it does not refund past ones, so also cancel the subscription with the company.
guides.caution: Loan repayment mandates cannot be cancelled from the UPI app; contact the lender. If you lost money to a scam, call 1930 or report at cybercrime.gov.in and inform your bank right away.

guides.title: "Virus detected" alerts on your phone? Block the website notifications in Chrome
guides.summary: Those "Virus detected", "Bill overdue" or "Police notice" pop-ups usually come from a website that was once allowed to send notifications. The permission is not a virus, so a scan finds nothing, but the site can keep pushing fake alerts. Block the site in Chrome in under a minute.

steps.title: Find the site
steps.body: Swipe down to open the notification shade. The alert shows Chrome and the website's name. If the notification has an Unsubscribe button, tap it.

steps.title: Open Chrome's notification list
steps.body: Open Chrome > tap the three dots (More) at the top right > Settings > Site settings > Notifications. You will see every site that is allowed to send notifications.

steps.title: Block every site you do not know
steps.body: Tap each unknown site under Allowed and change it to Block. Keep only sites you really use, like your bank or work site.

steps.title: From now on, tap Block
steps.body: When a website asks to "show notifications" (often disguised as "tap Allow to continue" or "to prove you are not a robot"), tap Block.

guides.tip: On some phones the path is Chrome > three dots > Settings > Notifications, which lists the same sites. Chrome also removes the permission automatically from some sites you never interact with.
guides.caution: Never tap the alert itself and never install a "cleaner" or "antivirus" app that the alert pushes. If you already shared bank details or paid money, call 1930 or report on cybercrime.gov.in.

guides.title: Check who is still logged into your WhatsApp, and log them out
guides.summary: Closing a browser tab does not log you out of WhatsApp Web. A linked computer keeps working even when your phone is offline, and WhatsApp only disconnects it after 30 days of inactivity. Open Linked devices, look at the list, and log out anything you do not recognise. Takes under a minute.

steps.title: Open Linked devices
steps.body: Android: open WhatsApp, tap the three-dot menu at the top right, then Linked devices. iPhone: open WhatsApp, tap Settings at the bottom right, then Linked devices.

steps.title: Read the list
steps.body: Each row is a computer, browser or tablet that is signed into your account, with the time it was last active. Anything you do not recognise, or any place you only used once (a cyber cafe, an office PC, a friend's laptop), should not be there.

steps.title: Log out the device
steps.body: Tap the device you want to remove, then tap Log out. The row disappears and that computer is signed out of your account. Repeat for every device you do not recognise.

steps.title: Make it a habit
steps.body: Check this list about once a month. WhatsApp allows up to four linked devices at a time, disconnects a linked device after 30 days of inactivity, and logs linked devices out if your phone itself is not used for more than 14 days. Turn on WhatsApp notifications so you are told when a new device is linked.

guides.tip: If you have to use WhatsApp Web on a computer that is not yours, use a private or incognito window and log out manually from the web page before you leave. Closing the tab or shutting the browser is not a log out.
guides.caution: A linked device can read your chats and send messages as you. On 18 November 2026 the National Cyber Crime Threat Analytics Unit, under the Home Ministry's I4C, issued an advisory, Safe Use of WhatsApp Web, telling people to log out after every session and not to use WhatsApp Web on cyber cafes, public kiosks, hotel business centres or borrowed computers. If your account has been misused, report it at cybercrime.gov.in or call 1930.

guides.title: Stop strangers adding you (or your parents) to WhatsApp scam groups
guides.summary: Leaving a 'stock tips' or 'profit' group does not stop the next one. One WhatsApp privacy setting means only your contacts can add you to groups; everyone else can only send an invite you can ignore.

steps.title: Open Privacy
steps.body: Open WhatsApp > Settings > Privacy. (On Android, Settings is in the three-dot menu at the top right; on iPhone it is the Settings tab at the bottom.)

steps.title: Change who can add you to groups
steps.body: Tap Groups. Change Everyone to My contacts (or My contacts except... to exclude some contacts too). Confirm. Now only people saved in your contacts can add you directly.

steps.title: Ignore invites from unknown numbers
steps.body: If someone not allowed tries to add you, they can only send a group invite in a private chat. It expires after 3 days. Do not open invites from numbers you do not know. If you are still added to a group by someone outside your contacts, WhatsApp shows a safety overview screen where you can leave the group straight away.

steps.title: Silence unknown callers
steps.body: Settings > Privacy > Calls > turn on Silence unknown callers. Calls from numbers not in your contacts will not ring, but they still appear in your Calls list.

guides.tip: Do this on your parents' phones too: it takes under a minute and stops most stock-tip and 'task job' group spam at the source.
guides.caution: No real investment advisor adds strangers to WhatsApp groups promising fixed profits. Never pay into an app or account shared in such a group. If you lost money, call 1930 or report at cybercrime.gov.in.

guides.title: Someone reposted your reel? Turn on Instagram Content Protection
guides.summary: Instagram's Content Protection (announced 17 November 2026) scans Instagram and Facebook for copies of your original videos and lets you hide them or add a credit link back to you. It is rolling out to eligible creators first.

steps.title: Check if you have it
steps.body: Eligible creators get a notification about Content Protection in their activity feed (the heart icon). You can also look under Your professional tools in the app. Not everyone has it yet: Instagram says eligibility is based on its originality and integrity standards.

steps.title: Enroll once
steps.body: Open the notification or Content protection in Your professional tools and enroll. From then on, every original video you post is protected automatically. Older eligible reels can be added by selecting them by hand.

steps.title: Decide what to do with each copy
steps.body: When a match is found you see the copy, its views and the account's follower count. Choose Track (watch it, the default), Hide from everyone (it can no longer be viewed on Instagram and Facebook), Add credit link (an "original by" label linking to your reel, for matches on Instagram) or Release (drop the claim).

steps.title: Add accounts you allow
steps.body: Put your second account, collaborators or brands you licensed your video to on the allow list, so their posts are not flagged as copies.

guides.tip: Not eligible yet? Report a copy yourself through Instagram's Intellectual Property reporting form (help.instagram.com). It works, but you have to find and report each copy one by one.
guides.caution: The feature is rolling out gradually and menu names may differ by app version. Detection of AI-made copies that reuse your spoken words is only being tested with a small group of creators. Only claim videos you made yourself.

guides.title: Wedding card on WhatsApp is an .apk? Turn off "Install unknown apps"
guides.summary: A real wedding invitation is a PDF, photo or video. A file ending in .apk is an app, and fake invite apps are used to steal OTPs and empty bank accounts. Four steps to block them on Android.

steps.title: Check the file before you tap
steps.body: Look at the end of the file name. Wedding_Card.pdf or .jpg is a card. Wedding_Card.apk is an app: do not open it. If it came from a friend or relative, call them and ask if they sent it.

steps.title: Turn off "Install unknown apps" for WhatsApp, Chrome and Files
steps.body: Open Settings and search for "Install unknown apps" (on Pixel: Settings > Apps > Special app access > Install unknown apps). Tap WhatsApp and turn "Allow from this source" off. Do the same for Chrome, Files and any other app that shows Allowed.

steps.title: Keep Play Protect scanning on
steps.body: Open the Play Store > tap your profile icon (top right) > Play Protect > Settings (gear) > turn on "Scan apps with Play Protect".

steps.title: If the phone says Install blocked, stop there
steps.body: Tap Cancel. Do not tap Settings, even if the sender tells you to: that is the trick. If you already installed it: turn off mobile data and Wi-Fi, uninstall the app, call your bank to block cards and UPI, change your PINs, and call 1930 or report at cybercrime.gov.in.

guides.tip: Do this on your parents' phones too. Most new Android phones keep "Install unknown apps" off by default, so if WhatsApp shows Allowed, someone turned it on.
guides.caution: Menu names differ slightly by phone brand and Android version; searching "Install unknown apps" in Settings works on most phones. iPhones cannot install .apk files, but the same rule applies to unknown links.

guides.title: CapCut is banned in India: which free editor to use for Reels
guides.summary: CapCut has been blocked in India since June 2020. Skip the APK. VN is a good free option, and for Reels the best free pick is Edits, Instagram's own editor.

steps.title: Do not download a CapCut APK
steps.body: CapCut is not on the Play Store or App Store in India. Fake CapCut sites and installers have been used to steal passwords and logins. Install apps only from the Play Store or App Store.

steps.title: Good option: VN Video Editor
steps.body: Free, and exports without a watermark. A paid Pro tier exists but is optional.

steps.title: Best for Reels: install Edits
steps.body: Open the Play Store or App Store, search Edits (by Instagram) and install it. It is free and available on Android and iPhone.

steps.title: Log in and add your video
steps.body: Sign in with your Instagram account, start a new project and import your clips (or record in the app).

steps.title: Captions, music, export
steps.body: Add auto captions, pick music from Instagram's library, then export without a watermark: save to your phone or share straight to Instagram.

guides.tip: Edits also has a free Mac app (Apple Silicon, M1 or later) since November 2026. There is no Windows version yet.
guides.caution: Never install a video editor from a link or an APK file. Menu names in Edits can change with app updates, and Edits needs an Instagram account.

guides.title: Lock your Aadhaar fingerprint in 2 minutes (Biometric Lock)
guides.summary: With a cloned fingerprint, a fraudster can try to withdraw cash from an Aadhaar-linked bank account through AePS, without any OTP. Locking your Aadhaar biometrics makes fingerprint and iris checks fail until you unlock them.

steps.title: Log in to myAadhaar
steps.body: Type myaadhaar.uidai.gov.in into your browser yourself (do not open links from messages). Tap Login, enter your 12-digit Aadhaar number and the captcha, then the OTP sent to your Aadhaar-linked mobile number. Your mobile number must be registered with Aadhaar.

steps.title: Open Lock/Unlock Biometrics
steps.body: Under Aadhaar Services, tap 'Lock/Unlock Biometrics'. Tick the box that says you understand biometric authentication will not work until you unlock, then tap Lock (on some screens 'Enable'). You will see a confirmation that your biometrics are locked.

steps.title: Need your fingerprint at a bank or ration shop? Unlock for 10 minutes
steps.body: Go back to the same Lock/Unlock Biometrics page, log in with OTP and choose Unlock. The unlock is temporary: after about 10 minutes the lock turns on again by itself. Use 'Disable' only if you want to switch the lock off completely.

steps.title: If money is taken
steps.body: Call 1930 (National Cybercrime Helpline) at once, or report at cybercrime.gov.in, and inform your bank.

guides.tip: Do it for your parents and grandparents too: anyone whose Aadhaar is linked to a bank account. The new Aadhaar app from UIDAI also lets you lock and manage biometrics.
guides.caution: Screen labels can change slightly; always follow the official UIDAI site. OTP-based Aadhaar checks still work while biometrics are locked. UIDAI never asks for your OTP on a call.

guides.title: Reel sharp on your phone but blurry on Instagram? 3 fixes
guides.summary: Instagram compresses every upload. These three fixes keep your reels as sharp as possible: one setting in the app, the right export size, and a clean upload.

steps.title: Turn on Upload at highest quality
steps.body: In the Instagram app: Profile > Menu (three lines, top right) > Settings and privacy > under 'Your app and media' tap 'Media quality' (on some versions 'Data usage and media quality') > turn on 'Upload at highest quality'. On the same screen, turn off 'Use less mobile data' / Data saver if it is on. Instagram notes uploads may take a little longer.

steps.title: Export at 1080 x 1920, 30 fps
steps.body: Export your reel as a vertical 9:16 MP4 (H.264) at 1080 x 1920 pixels and 30 frames per second. A 4K file gives no benefit: Instagram scales it down and it can look softer. Our own reels are made at 1080 x 1920, 30 fps.

steps.title: Upload the original file on good WiFi
steps.body: Upload on a strong WiFi or 5G connection, not a weak mobile signal. Use the original exported file. Do not upload a copy that was sent through WhatsApp or downloaded from another app: WhatsApp compresses videos, so the quality is already lost before Instagram compresses it again.

guides.tip: Send this to the friend whose reels always look blurry. Check a new upload after a few minutes: the sharp version can take a moment to appear.
guides.caution: Menu names can differ slightly by app version. These steps reduce quality loss; they cannot stop Instagram's own compression, and they do not change reach.

guides.title: Courier asked you to dial a code? Stop the call forwarding scam in 4 steps
guides.summary: Scammers posing as couriers, banks or your telecom company ask you to dial a short code. It quietly forwards your calls, including bank OTP and verification calls, to their phone. Here is how to spot it, check it and switch it off.

steps.title: Never dial a code a stranger gives you
steps.body: Do not dial any code sent by an unknown caller or SMS, especially codes that start with 21, 61 or 67 followed by a phone number (for example *21*<number>#). *21* turns on forwarding of all your calls. Common excuses: 'your parcel is stuck', 'KYC pending', 'your SIM will be blocked'.

steps.title: Check whether call forwarding is on
steps.body: Android: open the Phone app > three-dot menu > Settings > Call forwarding (on some phones it is under Calls, or Calling accounts > your SIM > Call forwarding). iPhone: Settings > Phone > Call Forwarding (on newer iOS: Settings > Apps > Phone > Call Forwarding). If 'Always forward' is on to a number you do not know, something is wrong. Calls suddenly not reaching you is also a warning sign.

steps.title: Switch all forwarding off
steps.body: Dial ##002# and press call. This cancels all call forwarding (the code the I4C advisory recommends). On Jio, *402 cancels forwarding of all calls. You can also turn the switch off in the settings screen from step 2. If the code does not work, call your operator's customer care.

steps.title: Lost money? Report at once
steps.body: Call the national cyber helpline 1930 or file a complaint at cybercrime.gov.in, and inform your bank. Reporting within the first hours gives the best chance to freeze the money.

guides.tip: Send this to parents and grandparents who often get calls from couriers. A real courier never needs you to dial a code.
guides.caution: Codes and menu names can differ by operator, phone model and software version. Never share an OTP with anyone on a call.

guides.title: Hindi and English captions on the same reel: Bilingual captions in Edits, 4 steps
guides.summary: Meta's free Edits app can write your captions in a second language automatically, so a Hindi reel can show Hindi and English captions together. It takes four taps, and you should read every line before you post.

steps.title: Get the Edits app
steps.body: Install Edits by Meta from Google Play (Android) or the App Store (iPhone). The app is free. If you already have it, update it first: new features reach different app versions at different times.

steps.title: Add your video and tap Captions
steps.body: Start a new project and add the clip where you speak. Tap the Captions button in the bottom toolbar.

steps.title: Turn on Bilingual captions and pick the second language
steps.body: Tap Bilingual captions. Select a secondary language from the list, for example English for a Hindi reel. Meta lists 15 languages: English, Hindi, Bengali, Gujarati, Kannada, Spanish, Portuguese, Korean, Japanese, French, German, Indonesian, Russian, Italian and Thai.

steps.title: Tap Generate captions, then check every line
steps.body: Tap Generate captions. The second language is a machine translation, so read every line, fix wrong words and names, and only then export and post.

guides.tip: Keep the captions in the middle of the screen, above the bottom area where Instagram shows your name and caption text.
guides.caution: Button names can differ slightly between app versions. If you do not see Bilingual captions, update Edits. Translations can be wrong, so always check them before posting.

guides.title: Pension life certificate from home: Jeevan Pramaan face scan in 4 steps
guides.summary: Pensioners can give their yearly life certificate (Jeevan Pramaan) from an Android phone with a face scan, without going to the bank. The 2026 campaign runs from 1 to 30 November. A family member can do it on their own phone with the pensioner present.

steps.title: Install two apps from Google Play
steps.body: On an Android phone, open Google Play and install Jeevan Pramaan (the face authentication app) and AadhaarFaceRD (UIDAI's face capture service). AadhaarFaceRD has no icon on the home screen; that is normal, it runs in the background (you can see it under Settings, Apps). The official manual asks for Android 9 or newer, a 5 MP or better camera and an internet connection.

steps.title: Register the operator once
steps.body: Open Jeevan Pramaan. On Device Registration and Operator Identification, the person running the phone (a son, daughter, or the pensioner) enters their Aadhaar number, mobile number and email, enters the OTP, adds their name, ticks consent and taps Scan. Keep the face inside the circle and blink when asked. This is a one-time step per phone.

steps.title: Enter the pensioner's details
steps.body: On Pensioner Identification, enter the pensioner's Aadhaar number and mobile number and the OTP sent to that mobile. Then fill or check the PPO number, pension account number, bank details, Pension Sanctioning Authority and Pension Disbursing Authority. Check the preview carefully (wrong details lead to rejection), tick both boxes and tap Submit.

steps.title: Scan the pensioner's face and save the Pramaan ID
steps.body: Tick consent and tap Scan. The pensioner looks straight at the camera in good, even light, with eyes open, a neutral face and clear glasses only. On success the screen shows a Pramaan ID and an SMS with the ID and a download link arrives. Later, download the certificate at jeevanpramaan.gov.in to check whether the pension office accepted it.

guides.tip: Do it well before 30 November. Pensioners aged 80 and above could submit from 1 October. If the app does not work for you, the bank branch, post office (India Post Payments Bank) or a Common Service Centre can do it.
guides.caution: No bank or government office asks for an OTP or PIN on a phone call. If someone calls saying the pension will stop unless you share an OTP, it is fraud: hang up and call 1930 or report at cybercrime.gov.in. Install apps only from Google Play. Screen labels can change slightly with app versions; follow the official manual.

guides.title: Reel music muted (Audio unavailable)? 3 rules to keep your sound
guides.summary: If your reel says Audio unavailable, a copyright system usually removed the song. Three habits keep your music safe: add songs inside Instagram, use the right account type, and use royalty-free music for promotions. We also show how we make our own background music.

steps.title: Add the song inside Instagram
steps.body: In the Reels editor, tap the music (audio) option and pick a song from Instagram's own library. Songs mixed into the video in another editing app, or downloaded from YouTube or Spotify, are a common reason reels get muted.

steps.title: Check your account type
steps.body: Business accounts get only commercially licensed audio, a much smaller library. If you are a creator, not a shop: open your profile, tap the menu (three lines), then Account type and tools (on some versions Business tools and controls), then Switch account type, then Switch to creator account. Menu labels can differ slightly by app version.

steps.title: Use royalty-free music for promos
steps.body: For a shop, brand or paid promotion, do not use popular film songs. Business accounts see Meta's royalty-free Sound Collection in the same music picker; it is cleared for Facebook and Instagram only. For YouTube videos, use YouTube Studio, then Audio library, and filter by Attribution not required (Creative Commons tracks need a credit in the description).

steps.title: Or make your own music
steps.body: We make the background music for our reels ourselves with a small script that synthesises lo-fi chords and a beat (engine/lofi.py in our public repo github.com/veereshkumbar/technibaba-reels). Music you create yourself has no other rights owner.

guides.tip: If a reel is already muted, edit it with a song from Instagram's library or repost it with cleared audio. If you think the mute was a mistake, you can appeal in the app.
guides.caution: Even songs from Instagram's library can be muted later if the rights change. Do not switch a business account just to use popular songs in ads or brand posts: commercial use needs licensed music. This is general platform guidance, not legal advice.

guides.title: How to check which SIM cards are issued in your name (Sanchar Saathi)
guides.summary: Someone can get a SIM card using your ID without you knowing. The government's Sanchar Saathi website shows every mobile number registered in your name, and lets you report the ones that are not yours. It takes about 2 minutes.

steps.title: Open the official Sanchar Saathi website
steps.body: Type sancharsaathi.gov.in in your browser yourself (do not use links from messages). Go to Citizen Centric Services, then choose Know Mobile Connections in Your Name. The same option is in the Sanchar Saathi app.

steps.title: Log in with your mobile number and OTP
steps.body: Enter your 10-digit mobile number and the captcha (if shown), then enter the OTP sent to that number. Use a number that is active and in your own name.

steps.title: Check the list of numbers
steps.body: The page shows every mobile number registered against your identity, across all operators. Go through it slowly. Most people can have at most 9 connections in their name (6 in Jammu and Kashmir, Assam and the North-Eastern states).

steps.title: Report what is not yours, or not needed
steps.body: For a number you never took, select Not My Number. For an old number of yours that you no longer use, select Not Required. Then press Report. You get a ticket or reference number; the operator verifies the request and disconnects the number. Check again after a few weeks.

guides.tip: Do the same check for your parents and grandparents, using their phone for the OTP. Older family members are often the ones whose documents get misused.
guides.caution: Sanchar Saathi never asks for your bank details, card number or UPI PIN. If a SIM in your name was used for fraud, report it at cybercrime.gov.in or call 1930. Screen labels can change slightly; follow the wording on the official site.

guides.title: The first 3 seconds: our reel hook formula (with our own numbers)
guides.summary: On one of our reels 75% of viewers skipped in the first 3 seconds; on another only 26% did. Three things were different. These are our own Insights numbers, not a guarantee.

steps.title: Show the result in frame 0
steps.body: The first frame is also the thumbnail. Put the payoff there (a number, a result, a before/after) with a 3-5 word headline. Do not open with a logo, an intro or a greeting.

steps.title: Ask a question or make a claim within 1.5 seconds
steps.body: The first line should land within 1.5 seconds: a question, a disagreement or a surprising number. Put the same words on screen, because many people watch reels muted.

steps.title: Keep it short: 35-45 seconds
steps.body: On our 60-second test reels, viewers stayed for only 7-12 seconds. We now make 35-45 second reels and deliver the payoff before the 80% mark.

steps.title: Check your own numbers
steps.body: In each reel's Insights, look at the skip rate (how many people swiped away in the first 3 seconds) and the average watch time, and compare every new reel with the previous one. End with a prompt to send the reel to a friend: according to Instagram head Adam Mosseri, the top three ranking signals are watch time, likes and sends.

guides.tip: One reel, one idea. Whatever you want to show goes in the first frame.
guides.caution: These numbers come from our small channel (November 2026). Every channel is different; there is no guarantee of views or followers.

guides.title: Real or fake Wi-Fi? Three checks before you connect
guides.summary: At an airport, cafe or station, if you see two Wi-Fi networks with the same name, run these three checks before you connect.

steps.title: Match the name exactly
steps.body: Ask staff for the exact network name, or check the official sign, ticket or receipt. If even one character differs (for example a zero instead of the letter O in Airport), it is fake. If two networks have the same name, confirm with staff before connecting.

steps.title: Look at what the login page asks for
steps.body: Genuine public Wi-Fi usually asks only for a mobile number and OTP, or a room or ticket number. If the page asks for a bank password, card number, UPI PIN or email password, close it immediately. It is a fake page.

steps.title: Take browser warnings seriously
steps.body: If the browser shows 'Your connection is not private' or 'Not secure', tap 'Go back'. Never tap 'Proceed'.

steps.title: If you already connected
steps.body: Open your phone's Wi-Fi settings, tap the network and choose 'Forget this network'. Change any password you entered right away and turn on two-step verification for that account.

guides.tip: Outside home, do banking and payments only on mobile data. Use free Wi-Fi only for browsing.
guides.caution: This is a general safety guide. If you lose money, call your bank immediately and report it at cybercrime.gov.in or on the 1930 helpline (India).

guides.title: Free airport Wi-Fi can be a trap
guides.summary: An open Wi-Fi network without a password can be a fake hotspot set up to steal passwords. Here is the simple rule that keeps you safe.

steps.title: Understand the risk
steps.body: Anyone can create a hotspot with an official-sounding name (for example Free_Airport_WiFi_Fast). Once you connect, it can show a fake login page and capture your password.

steps.title: Bank only on mobile data
steps.body: In public places, use your own mobile data for UPI, net banking and online payments.

steps.title: Turn off auto-join
steps.body: In your phone's Wi-Fi settings, turn off auto-join for open networks so the phone does not connect to a fake network on its own.

steps.title: Learn to spot the real network
steps.body: See our guide on the three checks: the network name, the login page and browser warnings.

guides.tip: Free Wi-Fi is for browsing. Money goes over mobile data.
guides.caution: This is a general safety guide. If you are defrauded, call your bank immediately and report it at cybercrime.gov.in or on the 1930 helpline (India).
